root_cause: The native 'cancel' event (fired on Escape in modal dialogs) is not included in Bootstrap's nativeEvents set, causing the EventHandler to treat it as a non-native event. This leads to inconsistent preventDefault behavior on repeated Escape presses. Additionally, the _cancelHandler may not guarantee event.preventDefault() execution under all conditions, allowing the dialog to close on the third Escape press when keyboard:false.
repair_strategy: Add 'cancel' to the nativeEvents set in dom/event-handler.ts so the EventHandler correctly recognizes and handles the native cancel event. Wrap the _cancelHandler logic in a try/finally block in dialog-base.ts to guarantee event.preventDefault() is always called, preserving the existing conditional behavior.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will consistently not dismiss the dialog when keyboard:false, allowing users to press Escape repeatedly without losing focus or closing the dialog, preserving keyboard operability and meeting WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Adding 'cancel' to nativeEvents is a safe internal change; it only affects event normalization.
The try/finally introduces negligible overhead; no functional change is expected.
When keyboard:true, Escape continues to close the dialog after preventDefault.
Static backdrop transition still occurs when keyboard:false.
Dialog can still be dismissed via the Cancel transfer button or by submitting a valid OTP.
verification_requirements: Press Escape any number of times while the dialog is open with keyboard:false and backdrop:static; the dialog must remain open and focus must stay on the OTP input.
Verify that the static backdrop transition (visual 'bounce') still occurs on Escape presses when keyboard:false.
When keyboard:true, pressing Escape once must close the dialog and move focus back to the trigger button.
Confirm that the Cancel transfer button still sets status to 'Cancelled' and closes the dialog.
Confirm that submitting a valid six‑digit OTP sets status to 'Sent' and closes the dialog.
